text.en:
Kavya left a steel spoon in a hot cup of tea. After a minute the handle was hot too.
"How did the heat reach my hand?" she asked.
"Heat flows along the metal," said her aunt. "A wooden spoon would stay cool."

Heat is a form of energy. It always flows from a hotter object to a colder object until both are at the same temperature.
Materials that let heat pass easily are good conductors, such as metals. Materials that do not, such as wood, plastic and cloth, are poor conductors or insulators.
That is why pots are made of metal with plastic or wooden handles. Woollen clothes keep us warm because they hold in the heat of our body.
Heat always flows from a hot object to a cold object.
Metals let heat pass easily. They are good conductors.
Wood, plastic and cloth do not let heat pass easily. They are insulators.
Pots have metal bodies and plastic handles for this reason.

problem.en: Why does a steel spoon in hot tea become hot but a wooden spoon does not?

text.en: Heat flows from the hot tea into the spoon.
Steel is a good conductor, so heat travels quickly along it.
Wood is an insulator, so heat does not travel easily.

why.en: So the wooden spoon stays cool.

prompt.en: A friend says a woollen sweater makes you warm because it produces heat. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: A sweater does not make heat.
It is an insulator that keeps the heat of your body from escaping.

points.en: Heat flows from hot to cold.
Metals are good conductors; wood and plastic are insulators.
Insulators keep things warm or cool.
